findings.title: Historical PostgreSQL peak makes the unchanged acceptance predicate fail
findings.evidence: All four PostgreSQL observations record 537141248 bytes versus 536870912 configured, already present before seed and identical to the original failed report. New max events total 164089, with 1679380/1679363 microseconds some/full pressure and no captured swap/OOM.
findings.interpretation: The historical overshoot is isolated; adequate memory headroom is not established. memory.max may transiently overshoot and memory.peak is a lifetime maximum. File accounting dominates these snapshots and includes shared memory; it is not all private heap or necessarily reclaimable cache.
findings.disposition: Keep both failures intact. Review a versioned operational memory criterion before further acceptance runs; do not reset counters, increase memory or relax the existing validator to force a pass.

findings.title: UTC and monotonic durations diverge by 14174.818 seconds
findings.evidence: The closed report spans 18:49:56.268490 to 23:12:44.128825 UTC on October 22. Consecutive observations show gaps even inside after_seed, while monotonic time advances only fractions of a second.
findings.interpretation: The 26.55-minute figure is the recorded monotonic duration, not total UTC elapsed time. The report does not establish the cause, uninterrupted execution, SQL latency or performance relative to the earlier 46.814-second run.
findings.disposition: Obtain narrowly scoped read-only clock/power evidence from mac24 and add explicit clock coherence, per-operation timing and awake-lifecycle controls to a new protocol before any performance comparison.

limits: This primary audit verifies closed evidence and code; it does not query mac24 or recompute H&M private profiles.
Snapshots and cgroup deltas describe service activity between captures, including potential background work; they do not identify a SQL query as the cause or constitute isolated per-operation peaks.
Zero peak growth does not imply zero interval peaks. memory.stat shmem overlaps file accounting; do not add it as a disjoint category or equate file with fully reclaimable cache.
No CPU, disk-wait, SQL phase timing, sleep log or host clock implementation is present. Do not use the anomalous intervals as latency, pressure percentages or throughput benchmarks.
The replay checks four parity requests and four events; it is not exhaustive browser acceptance or sustained load. T8 remains pending.
Historical failed reports are not upgraded by this review or a future acceptance revision. T5/E4 and quality_accepted remain open/false.
